newsitem.title: USA: JP Stevens restructuring to eliminate debt.
newsitem.headline: JP Stevens restructuring to eliminate debt.

text.p: JPS Textile Group has reached an agreement with debt holders that would restructure the company, eliminating the public debt incurred at the time of the 1988 leveraged buyout of J.P. Stevens & Co, chief executive Jerry Hunter said Friday.
The agreement would create a new capital structure while the company's operating units continued business as usual, alleviating uncertainties associated with upcoming debt maturities, he said.

As a result, Hunter continued, JPS Textile will have the financial resources to make capital investments in its operating businesses to better position the company for long-term profitability and growth.
Under the terms of the agreement, all of JPS Textile's outstanding bond debt will be exchanged for substantially all the reorganized company's common stock, it said.

JPS said it has an agreement in principle with an unofficial committee of bondholders, representing more than 60 percent of its outstanding public debt, to convert 100 percent of its long-term debt to equity.
The restructuring is subject to formal documentation which the company expects to complete shortly.
Under the proposal, the restructuring will be effected through a voluntary, prepackaged chapter 11 filing which will not include its operating subsidiaries.

Under the restructuring, JPS Textile said, its operating subsidiaries will have a new revolving credit facility, which is expected to have provisions no less favorable than the existing facility and provide significant working capital.

In the meantime, the existing facility has been extended through July 16 to enable the company to complete the prepackaged Chapter 11 filing. If JPS Textile starts a Chapter 11 case by that date, the revolving credit facility will be extended automatically to the earlier of November 1 or the effective date of a reorganization.
The agreement also calls for the election of a new board.
JPS Textile said management has agreed to enter into new employment agreements in connection with the restructuring.

Specifically, the agreement calls for holders of JPS Textile's 10.25 percent senior subordinated notes and 10.85 percent senior subordinated discount notes to receive $10-$14 million in cash, contingent notes issued by JPS Capital Corp, and 93.29 percent of the new common stock.
The company said holders of the 7 percent subordinated debentures will receive 5.95 percent of the new common and senior management will receive 0.75% in lieu of their contractual retention payments.

The face amounts of JPS Textile's outstanding bond debt are $76,773,000 on its senior subordinated notes; $109,247,000 on its senior subordinated discount notes; and $54,071,000 on its subordinated debentures.
It said the notes from JPS Capital, a JPS Textile subsidiary, provid payment of up to $33-$37 million plus interest upon the occurrence of certain events.

The agreement in principle also provides that JPS Textile's existing senior preferred stock will be exchanged for warrants to purchase common stock of the reorganized company. The existing junior preferred stock and common stock will be cancelled.
Spokeswoman Wendi Kopsick said 34 percent of the common is held by Odyssey Partners and 17 percent by Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette.

With annual revenues of about $450 million, JPS Textile is one of the largest domestic manufacturers of textile and textile related products for the apparel fabric, industrial and home fashion markets. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
